why_the_full_suite: A deployment change is MANDATORY_FULL by doctrine: what the record claims is served must be what a fresh assembly builds, and nothing narrower proves it.

true_new_failures.tests/pettripfinder/test_global_assemble: EXPECTED EPOCH MOVE. The test enumerates the founder-authorized selection. Toledo joins it as the eleventh by a named founder decision, so the list gained TOLEDO. It is still enumerated, not counted, so a market admitted without a decision still fails.
EXPECTED EPOCH MOVE. Same enumerated selection, same single entry added.
true_new_failures.tests/pettripfinder/test_grand_rapids_la: EXPECTED EPOCH MOVE, and the one that matters. This guard exists to catch a market being swept into the authorized set without a founder decision. It allowed exactly one admission after 032; there have now been two, Cincinnati and Toledo. The allowed set is ENUMERATED by market id rather than relaxed to a count, so its force is unchanged.

closure.how: The fix is a TEST_EXPECTATION_CHANGE over two ordinary modules, which regression_delta classifies as narrow: no row of the matrix makes a second broad regression mandatory. Closure is proved by NODE ID over the 30 modules the classifier named, not by re-running the suite for bookkeeping.
closure.note: All three are in the f75aa95 baseline AND were failing in this broad run before the fix. They read capture artifacts under data/acquisition/ that this worktree does not carry. Nothing about them moved.

verdict: CLEAN -- the three TRUE_NEW_FAILUREs were expected epoch moves of enumerated authorized-set guards, each closed by naming the founder decision that admitted Toledo rather than by weakening the guard. TRUE_NEW_FAILURE = 0.
